column2: In the middle he should write the mantra with its power, enclosing it with the Shri seed — the wheel named "Kalantaka", giver of ease to gods and demons.
He should inscribe the wheel on birch-bark; it wards off all enemies; merely by wearing it one becomes victorious everywhere.
Now I shall tell the one called "Jvalamalin" ("garlanded with flames"), giving all desires: the seed, "Om Bhagavate", then "Narasimhaya",
the words "Jvaline, Maline, Diptadamshtraya, Agnine", "Trayaya", "Sarvadi-rakshoghnaya"; "Naḥ sarvabhu..."
Harir vinashanaya, destroyer of all fevers; at the end of the name "daha daha" and "pacha pacha" he should say,
raksha raksha, armour and weapon and ending with "tha", beginning with Om: Jvalamalin is declared the best mantra of sixty-eight syllables.
The merit-giving and other (limbs) as stated before, with thirteen syllables; with the Pankti metre by eleven; with eighteen syllables,
by the "sun", "karana" and "vara", he should make the limbs. He should remember Nrihari Jvalamalin in the form as told before.
Chanting a hundred thousand, offering a tenth part with ghee of a tawny cow: this best mantra destroys terrible epilepsy, spirits and the like.
Prana, Maya, Nrisimha, Srishti, Brahmastra — a six-syllable great mantra, giving all desires.
Its sage is Brahma, metre Pankti, deity Nrikesari; the limbs are made with the seed rich in six long vowels.
He should do meditation and worship by the rule stated before; when this mantra is perfected, all success comes to men.
Beginning with the Rama seed, a thirty-three-syllable mantra in Anushtubh; the sage is Prajapati; the metre Anushtubh; the deity Lakshmi-Nrikesari.
The limbs are conceived by all the words; having thus placed the five limbs, he should perform self-protection.
Touching the right arm, he should chant the mantra of Sharabha: Om, heart, Shiva, "mahate sharabhaya";
ending with "agnipriya" — this mantra is declared for protection; or, after the Rama mantra, he should recite "ksha" twice.
Or he should carefully make protection with Keshava and the rest: "May Keshava protect my feet; Narayana my shanks;
may Madhava protect my waist, Govinda my secret parts; may Vishnu protect my navel and Madhusudana my belly;
may Trivikrama protect my thighs, Nara my heart; may Shridhara protect my throat and Hrishikesha my face;
may Padmanabha protect my breasts and Damodara my head." Having thus placed them on the limbs at the time of chanting, the practitioner
becomes fearless of spirits, vetalas, planets and demons. He should carefully place again, meditating attentively:
Having thus made protection, a man becomes unassailable. This is the rule for all groups of Nrihari mantras.
By the rule stated before, he should do all meditation, worship and so on. "Victory to you, lotus-eyed one; homage to you, creator of the universe;
homage to you, Hrishikesha; homage to you, Great Person." Having prayed, chanted and recited thus, he should dismiss the Lord.
When the mantra is perfected, the mantra-knower becomes a seat of prosperity. "Jaya jaya Shri Nrisimha" — this best mantra has eight syllables.
Its sage is Brahma, metre Gayatri; its deity is the glorious Jaya-Nrisimha, who grants all desires.
With the moon, cow, and the sky (letters), again with the moon, the wise should not make the six limbs with six long vowels.
Then he should meditate in the heart on the Lord Nrisimha, crowned with the moon:

O glorious Nrikesari-bodied, sole kinsman of the world, O blue-throated, ocean of mercy, king of Sama, fire-and-moon-eyed fierce-handed, bearer of Pinaka, moon-crested lord of Rama, protect me, O Vishnu.
Having meditated thus, the mantra-knower should chant eight hundred thousand, offer a tenth part with ghee and milk-rice, worship as before.
Om, Maya, at the end of his own seed "Karna-ugram vira", "Mahavishnu" he should say, "jvalantam sarvatomukham",
sphura sphura twice, "prasphura" twice, then "ghora-ghora-tara", "te tanurupa" with two "tha",
prachata prachata twice, "kaha kaha", "mada", "bandha bandha", "ghataya ghataya", then armour and weapon:
Nrisimham bhishanam bhadram mrityumrityum namamy aham — an eighty-five-syllable mantra, granting desires to worshippers.
Its sages are Aghora and Brahma; its metres Trishtubh and Anushtubh; the deity is held to be Ghora-Nrisimha.
The wise should do its meditation and worship by Anushtubh rule. This best mantra is held especially to give all protection.
The seed, then "jaya jaya", then "Nrisimha" — eight syllables. The sage is Prajapati, the metre is declared Anushtubh,
the deity is Vidarana-Nrisimha ("tearing"); "jam" the seed, "ham" the power; application for obtaining all.
With the Nrisimha seed rich in long vowels he should perform the six-limb placing. He should meditate on the fierce Nrisimha tearing the enemy's chest,
with nails, tusks and weapons, giving fearlessness to devotees, abode of Shri, with hair like heated gold and blazing eyes,
touch of nails greater than the thunderbolt, divine lion, homage to you. The sage is declared Brahma, the metre Anushtubh,
the deity of this syllable-ocean is Divya-Nrikesari. With four feet and all, he should make the five limbs.
All meditation, worship and the rest has been told before, O lord of sages. All the things stated before become successful.
Om, "namo Bhagavate Narasimhaya", the heart; "jastejase avir avir bhava vajranakha"...
vajradamshtra karmanta, "asaya akrandaya" twice, "tamo grasa" twice, then ending "svaha", then "abhayam",
(on) the Self, at the end the many; the mantra whose seed ends with "dhruva", of sixty-two syllables. Its sage and the rest are told as before.
Om, the Nrisimha seed, "namo Bhagavate", then "Narasimhaya" and Om, when the seed is that,
rupaya, Om and own seed, "Kurmarupaya" Om, seed; "Varaharupaya", Om, seed, then "Nrisimha-";
rupaya Om and own seed; at the end of "Vamana-rupaya"; "papa" and the three "dhruva" seed; "Ramaya" at the head of the Veda;
the seed "Krishnaya" at the end of Om, and then the seed "Kalkine"; "jaya jaya"; then at the end of Shaligrama, "nivasine",
Divya-simhaya in the dative, "Svayambhuh Purushaya" heart; Om, own seed: this gives great sovereignty.
The Nrisimha mantra of "kha-anka" syllables has the sage Atri; the metre is Atijagati; the deity of the mantra is told:
the Ten Incarnations, Nrihari; the seed "kham"; the power imperishable. Having made the limbs with the seed rich in six long vowels, he should contemplate:
Like many moons, his eyes turned on Lakshmi's face, with the ten incarnations — may Nrihari spread happiness.
Chanting ten thousand; the offering is a tenth part with milk-rice; he should worship on the seat stated before, conceiving the form from the root.
First the limbs, and then Matsya and the others on the petals in the directions; having worshipped Indra and the rest and Vajra and the rest, he attains his desire.
Now I shall tell the great mantra of a thousand syllables, hidden in the tantras: Om, Maya, Rama, Kama, the seed, then "krodha" word,
murte Nrisimha at the end, "mahapurusha" he should say; "pradhana-dharma-adharma" at the end "nigada",
nirmochana at the end, "kala", then "purusha" he should say; "kalantaka-sadrik toya" ... "sveshvara" at the end "sadrik jala",
shranta, at the end "nivishta", "chaitanya-chit-sada", then "bhasaka", at the end "kaladi-atita-nityodita",
udayastamaya-akranta-mahakarunika; stated for the four-petalled heart lotus: at the end of the petals "nivishtita",
chaitanyatman, "chatur-amandvadashatman", then "chaturvinshatman", "panchavinshatman" at the end;
Baka Hari at the end of "sahasra", "murte ehy ehi"; "Bhagavan Nrisimha Purusha Krodheshvara" with "rasa",
sravanditanta pada, "kalpantagni-sahasra", "koti-abha", "mahadeva", "nikaya-dasha";
shatayajnatala to be known, then a pair "amala-amala"; "pingalekshana-sata-damshtra", "damshtrayudha-nakhayudha",
danavendrantaka, "vahni-shonita"; "sam-sakti-vigraha"; "bhutapasmara-yatudhan" (spirits, epilepsy, demons),
suraasura-vandyamana-pada-pankaja, "Bhagavan vyomachakreshvara", "prabhavapyaya",
rupena uttishtha uttishtha; "avidya-nichayam daha daha" (burn the heap of ignorance); "jnana-aishvaryam", "prakashaya prakashaya",
Om sarvajna aroshanta, "jambha jrimbha", "avatara", "satyapurusha" at the end, "sadasan-madhya" he should say:
nivishtam mama duhsvapna-bhayam, "nigada", "bhayam kantara", "bhayam visha",
jvara, "dakini", "krityadhvare revatibhayam", "ashani", "bhayam durbhiksha-bhayam mari",
bhayam marica, "bhayam chhaya", "skanda-apasmara", "bhayam chora-bhayam",
jala-svapna-agni-bhayam, "gaja-simha-bhujanga", "bhayam janma-jara-marana" and so on:
bhayam nirmochaya twice, "prashamaya" twice, "jneya-rupa-dharana", "Nrisimha-brihatsama", ...
purusha at the end "sarvabhaya-nivarana"; eight-eights (sixty-four) "cheti-abhaya" he should say;
vidya-vrita, thirty-three crores of deities, "namita", "pada-pada-pankajanvita" he should say;
saha sravadana, "sahasrodara", "sahasrekshana", "sahasrapada";
sahasrabhuja, "sahasrajihva", "sahasta", "lalata", "sahasrayudha";
tamah-prakashaka, "puramathana", "sarva", "mantraraja-ishvara", "vihayasa-gati-prada",
patala-gati-prada, "yantra-mardana", "ghora-attahasa-hasita-vishva-avasa",
Vasudeva, then "akrura", then "hayamukha", "paramahamsa", "vishvesha", "vishva-vidambana",
nivishta, "pradurbhava-karaka", "Hrishikesha", "svachchhanda", "nihshesha-jiva",
grasaka, "maha", "pishita-asrik", "lampata", "khecari", "siddhyate pradayaka",
ajeya avyaya avyakta brahmanda-udara, then "brahma-sahasra", "koti-sragrunda",
mala-pandita-munda, "matsya kurma", "varaha-nrisimha-vamana",
trailokya-akramana, "pada-shalika", "rama-traya", "vishnu-rupa", "dhara",
tattva-traya, "pranava-adhara", "tat-shikha", "nivishta-vahni-jaya", "svadha", "vashat",
netra-varma-astra, "pranadhara", "adidevapada", "prana-apana", "nivishtita",
pancharatrika, "ditija-vinidhana", "kara", "mahamaya", "amogha", "darya", "daityendra",
darya, "dalana", "tejorashin", "dhruvam smara", "tejasvara", "purusha", "satyapurusha",
astra, "tara", "achyutastra", "tara", "vacha", "sudeva", "phat"; "tara", "maya", "murti", "phat", "vah", "kama";
murti-astra, "avyaya", "bija", "vishvamurti", "avyaya", "mayavishvatmane", "shat", "tara";
phat, "tara", "aham", "vishvarupin", "astra", "tara", "uhnai-paramanta", "hram", "sa", "phat", "pranava";
hrah, "hiranyagarbha-rupa", "dharana", "phat", "dhruva", "hraim", "anaupamya-rupa-dharin", "astra", "dhruva";
ksaim, "Nrisimha-rupa-dharin", "Om", "klam", "shlam"...; "ashtanga-vinyasa", "murti-dharin", "phat";
hrau, "nisarga-siddhi-eka-rupa-dharin", "phat", "tara", "varma-traya", "sankara", "vam", "amuka-mastaka";
khanda khanda, "khadaya khadaya", "klim", "sadhyam anaya" twice, then "mahatman", "samyag darshaya" twice,
the seed rich in six long vowels, "kshapita", "kalmasha", "uttaraya" twice, the five arrow-seeds he should say;
at the end of "Nrisimha", then "jvalatmane svaha" he should say; at the end of Nrisimha, then "kalatmane svaha", "dhruva";
the sky-seed, the Kama-seed, two Lakshmi-seeds, the ends Maya-Om: the mantra measured as a thousand syllables.
Its sage is Kapila, metre Jagati; the deity is Shri Lakshmi-Nrihari; the seed "ksaim", the power "Vahnivallabha" (svaha).
The colour is white, the tone udatta, as the wise say; the field is the Supreme Self; the application is for obtaining all.
Ksah sahasrabahave sahasrayudhadharaya Nrisimhaya agnijaya astraya phat — the mantra is declared.
With this, having purified the hands, he should perform the limbs: Om, "ksham", at the end of "sahasra", "kshara", "vijrimbhita";
Nrisimhaya agnijaya at the end — the heart mantra is declared. "Mara", "ksim", "mahatenu", "prabha", "vikara";
Nrisimhaya agnijaya at the end — the head mantra is declared. Om, "ksum", "taptayamhaya", at the end "adrik-kesha" he should say:
jvalati-avakala, "dirgha", "vajradhika", "nakha-sparsha", "divyasimha, homage to you, Lord Hari",
mahadhvasta jagadrupa Nrisimhaya twice, with this the tuft is told, then the armour.
Om, "ksaim", "suvarnam te", "madamatta"; "vihvalita-Nrisimhaya svaha": the armour is remembered.
Om, "rksau", "sahasraksha", "vishvasraksha", "vishvarupa", "dharana", "agnipriya" at the end: the eye mantra is declared.
Om, "ksha", at the end of "sahasra", "varavepa"; at the end of "sahasra", "yudhaya", "Nrisimhaya agnisundari" (svaha).
This is called the weapon mantra. Then he should meditate on Nrikesari, bright as a thousand rising suns, three-eyed, with fearful ornaments,
with very sharp-pointed arms and staffs, tearing the demons. Having meditated thus, the mantra-knower should chant a thousand with milk-rice,
and offer soaked in ghee; then the mantra is well perfected. On the Vaishnava seat stated before, conceiving the form from the root,
having worshipped Nrihari, he should first worship the limbs: the discus, conch, noose, goad, thunderbolt,
mace, sword, shield on the petals; then the lords of the worlds and Vajra and the rest.
When the mantra is perfected, the mantra-knower is fit to do applications: having consecrated ash, he should smear one seized by a planet;
merely by smearing with ash all planets are destroyed. By this same rule, yakshas, rakshasas, kinnaras,
spirits, ghosts and pishachas are destroyed, without doubt. Hostile rites done by others are neutralised by ash consecrated with this mantra;
smeared at once, the man becomes unassailable. On an auspicious day he should set a pot on the all-auspicious diagram,
fill it with holy water and chant a hundred and eight times; a man sprinkled with it surely crosses all calamity.
What need of saying more? This best mantra grants all desires. "Vajranakhaya vidmahe tikshnadamshtraya dhimahi; Tan no Nrisimhah prachodayat."
This is the Nrisimha Gayatri, granting all desired things; merely by remembering it all sin is destroyed.
While dance is going on all around, with sayings of victory and auspiciousness, fragrant with sandal, aloe, musk, camphor and the like,
with scent-bearers carrying the fragrance of many flowers, adorned with divine Gandharva women singing,
he should remember Raghava seated on a lion-throne above the Pushpaka aerial car, with Lakshmana and Sita, shining with matted hair and crown,
dark, bearing bow and arrows, with Sugriva and Vibhishana, having killed Ravana and come, who protected the three worlds.
Having meditated thus, the mantra-knower should chant the mantra a hundred thousand, offer a tenth part with ghee-soaked milk-rice and worship as before.
Om, the heart, "Sitapataye", then "Ramaya", "hana hana" twice, at the end armour, weapon, and "agnipriya".
This mantra of nineteen syllables accomplishes all aims. Its sage is Vishvamitra; the metre is declared Anushtubh;
the deity is Ramabhadra; the seed is "jam", the power "namah". Then, with the syllables arising from the mantra in order, he should meditate as before.
Its worship and the desire-rites are all like the six-syllable. Om, own seed, Kamala, he should recite "Ramabhadra",
after "maheshvasa", "Raghuvira", "nripottama", at the end of "dashasyantaka": "mam raksha dehi".
At the end of "parama" and "me shriyam syat" — the arrow-quality-syllable mantra, without seeds, of thirty-two syllables, is the giver of fruit.
Its sage is Vishvamitra; the metre is declared Anushtubh. Its deity is Ramabhadra; the seed is "sva", the power Indira.
The mantra-knower should make the limbs with the words beginning with the three seeds; having placed the five limbs, he should place the syllables in order:
on the head, forehead, eyes, ears, both cheeks, nose, mouth, both arm-joints, breasts, heart and navel in order;
on the waist, organ, anus, and the foot-joints he should place the mantra's syllables. Its meditation and worship should be done as before.
Three hundred thousand is the preliminary practice, with milk-rice offering. Meditating on Rama, yellow in colour, he should chant a hundred thousand attentively,
offering a tenth part with lotuses; with wealth he becomes lord of wealth. Om, Maya, two Rama (seeds), "Dasharathaya" and the heart:
an eleven-syllable mantra; its sage and worship are as before. "Trailokya-natha" at the end, ending in the heart, eight-syllabled:
its placing, meditation, worship and so on are all as before too. At the end of "Anjaneya", "guruve", ending in the heart.
